mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the African Union Summit and the UN Commission for Social Development.

List-I
 a. AUC Chair in 2026
 b. India’s leadership in the 64th UN Commission for Social Development
 c. Institutional framework of the Commission
 d. Declaration monitored by the Commission

List-II
 i. ECOSOC
 ii. Mahmoud Ali Youssouf
 iii. Copenhagen (1995) declaration
 iv. MoS, WCD

Codes:
 a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
 a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii
 a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
 a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
mcqs.explanation: The correct matching is AUC Chair—Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, India’s leadership—MoS WCD, institutional framework—ECOSOC, and monitored declaration—Copenhagen (1995). The tempting second code wrongly associates Mahmoud Ali Youssouf with India’s leadership.

mcqs.question: Who was India’s Sherpa at the First BRICS Sherpa Meeting held in New Delhi in February 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Sudhakar Dalela was India’s Sherpa at the First BRICS Sherpa Meeting in New Delhi. Prataprao Jadhav was associated with the International AYUSH Conference, while Mahmoud Ali Youssouf was the AUC Chair.

mcqs.question: Him-CONNECT, held during WSDS in New Delhi from 25–27 February 2026, showcased technologies from which organisation?
mcqs.explanation: Him-CONNECT showcased 24+ technologies of NMHS. NFDB was associated with the World Seafood Congress, NDB is a development bank, and INTACH produced the documentary on the Falcon Living Museum.

mcqs.question: Which organisation organised the 6th National Crop Nutrition Summit held at NSE, BKC, Mumbai?
mcqs.explanation: The 6th National Crop Nutrition Summit was organised by the Indian Micro-Fertilizers Manufacturers Association. IAFI was associated with the World Seafood Congress, while TERI hosted WSDS-related activities.

mcqs.question:
How many of the following statements about India’s seafood sector are correct?

1. India is the 2nd largest aquaculture producer.
2. India exported 1.78 million tonnes of seafood in 2023–24.
3. The export value in 2023–24 was $7.38 billion.
4. India accounted for about 12% of global shrimp trade.
mcqs.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India is the 2nd largest aquaculture producer and exported 1.78 million tonnes in 2023–24. Statement 3 changes the correct export value of $7.38 billion, and statement 4 changes India’s share of global shrimp trade from about 21% to 12%.

mcqs.question: Who among the following received the Peter Hovgate Award 2026 from India?
mcqs.explanation: Harini Ravi of India and Riza Jane Banicod of the Philippines received the Peter Hovgate Award 2026. Riza Jane Banicod was the other award recipient, whereas Sudhakar Dalela and Dilma Rousseff were associated with BRICS-related facts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was listed as a BRICS partner country in 2026?
mcqs.explanation: Vietnam was listed among the BRICS partner countries. Bangladesh, the UAE and Algeria were mentioned among the members of the New Development Bank, not as the BRICS partner-country list in this context.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the New Development Bank and BioAsia 2026.

List-I
 a. Establishment of the New Development Bank
 b. President of the New Development Bank
 c. New members of the New Development Bank
 d. BioAsia and Telangana’s associated vision

List-II
 i. 2014, Shanghai
 ii. Dilma Rousseff
 iii. Colombia and Uzbekistan
 iv. Hyderabad—“Life Sciences Capital of India”; Telangana’s $3 trillion by 2047 vision

Codes:
 a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
 a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
 a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv
 a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i
mcqs.explanation: The New Development Bank was established in 2014 at Shanghai, is headed by Dilma Rousseff, and has Colombia and Uzbekistan as new members. BioAsia is associated with Hyderabad as the “Life Sciences Capital of India” and Telangana’s $3 trillion by 2047 vision.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The MHA guidelines on “Vande Mataram” require all six stanzas to be observed at official functions and educational institutions and mark 150 years since its first publication.
Reason (R): “Vande Mataram” was first published on 7 November 1875.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are true, and the first-publication date of 7 November 1875 explains the reference to 150 years. The guidelines also specify all six stanzas at official functions and educational institutions.

mcqs.question: According to the February 2026 MHA guidelines, when is “Vande Mataram” played in relation to the President’s speeches and the arrival or departure of Governors and Lieutenant Governors?
options: Before or after the President’s speeches on AIR and Doordarshan, and when Governors or LGs arrive or leave
Only during the President’s speeches on AIR and Doordarshan
Only when Governors or LGs arrive, but not when they leave
At educational institutions but not on AIR and Doordarshan
mcqs.explanation: The guidelines provide for “Vande Mataram” before or after the President’s speeches on AIR and Doordarshan and when Governors or LGs arrive or leave. The other options incorrectly restrict the occasions or exclude broadcasting.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding heritage and archaeological findings in February 2026.

List-I
 a. Tyonda, Jhunjhunu
 b. Bhirrana
 c. Mature phase of the Bhirrana settlement
 d. Falcon Living Museum

List-II
 i. 2600–1900 BCE
 ii. Mizo heritage village near Aizawl documented by INTACH
 iii. 11th–12th century temple remains with Lakshmi and Ganesha
 iv. Fatehabad, Haryana

Codes:
 a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii
 a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii
 a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii
 a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii
mcqs.explanation: Tyonda yielded 11th–12th century temple remains associated with Lakshmi and Ganesha; Bhirrana is in Fatehabad, Haryana, and its mature phase dates to 2600–1900 BCE. The Falcon Living Museum is a Mizo heritage village near Aizawl documented by INTACH.

mcqs.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the Valley of the Kings, Chennakeshava Temple and heritage institutions.

List-I
 a. Inscriptions in the Valley of the Kings
 b. Occurrences of the name “Cikai Korran”
 c. Chennakeshava Temple, Belur
 d. ASI and INTACH institutional facts

List-II
 i. About 30 Indian inscriptions in Tamil-Brahmi, Prakrit and Sanskrit, dating to the 1st–3rd centuries CE
 ii. 8 times
 iii. Part of UNESCO’s “Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas” (2023)
 iv. ASI established in 1861; DG Yadubeer Singh Rawat; INTACH established in 1984

Codes:
 a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv
 a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii
 a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv
 a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i
mcqs.explanation: The Valley of the Kings contains about 30 Indian inscriptions from the 1st–3rd centuries CE, and “Cikai Korran” occurs 8 times. Chennakeshava Temple is part of UNESCO’s 2023 “Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas”; the ASI was established in 1861, its DG is Yadubeer Singh Rawat, and INTACH was established in 1984.
